instance.name: Decentralised Trust Graph — Credentials Task Force
instance.host: Trust over IP Foundation / Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust
instance.maintainer: Risk Assessment & Harms Prevention Task Force, DTGWG

risk.name: Genesis Policy Capture
risk.description: The initiator hard-codes biased, self-serving, or exclusionary policies at genesis before any oversight mechanism exists. Phase 1 concentrates all power in one person; these policies may persist and shape the entire community lifecycle.
risk.harm_description: Biased or discriminatory membership criteria embedded permanently; initiator retains unchecked authority; downstream decisions tainted by flawed genesis assumptions.

risk.name: Governance Transition Failure
risk.description: The initiator's elevated authority is never formally transitioned to the governing body or anchors. The VTC continues to depend on a single person for governance decisions beyond the bootstrapping period.
risk.harm_description: Single point of governance failure; community paralysed or captured if initiator unavailable, coerced, or acting in bad faith.

risk.name: Anchor Homogeneity / Collusion Cluster
risk.description: Trust anchors are selected from a single social, geographic, or organisational network, creating a homogeneous cluster that can collude, share bias, or be collectively coerced.
risk.harm_description: Coordinated anchor collusion enables mass fraudulent admissions; single-jurisdiction anchors vulnerable to state coercion; cultural bias embedded in vouching practices.

risk.name: Governance Bandwidth Exhaustion
risk.description: Governing body capacity is overwhelmed — naturally through growth or deliberately through bad-faith abuse of governance mechanisms.
risk.harm_description: Backlogs in admission, appeals, revocation; legitimate members denied timely due process; community trust in governance erodes.

risk.name: Sybil Identity Proliferation
risk.description: A malicious actor creates multiple M-DIDs and uses coordinated vouching to pass multi-VRC admission thresholds. Uniqueness enforcement is an explicitly open issue in the VTC Bootstrapping Draft.
risk.harm_description: Adversary gains disproportionate influence; voting and governance captured; legitimate members outvoted or silenced.

risk.name: Social Graph Privilege Exclusion
risk.description: The web-of-trust model structurally advantages applicants with pre-existing social connections. Those with non-dominant cultural backgrounds or limited digital literacy are disproportionately excluded.
risk.harm_description: Marginalised individuals unable to obtain required VRCs; VTC becomes homogeneous; human rights implications where VTC access enables civic or economic participation.

risk.name: IDVP Breach / Cascading Invalidation
risk.description: An IDVP suffers a data breach, is deregistered, or issues fraudulent IDVCs. Members admitted using those credentials face re-verification or revocation with no clear pathway.
risk.harm_description: Mass credential invalidation; personal identity data exposed; fraud ring may have obtained IDVCs through compromised IDVP; re-verification creates accessibility barriers.

risk.name: DID Document Manipulation
risk.description: An adversary manipulates DID documents to substitute or forge public keys, enabling impersonation of legitimate members or anchors. DID document storage is an open issue in the bootstrapping draft.
risk.harm_description: Fraudulent credential presentations accepted as genuine; impersonated anchors used to admit sybil members; member credentials stolen and replayed.

risk.name: M-DID Linkability Across VTCs
risk.description: If a member uses the same M-DID across VTCs, or if the trust registry exposes sufficient metadata, an adversary can construct a cross-community profile. **SPEC UPDATE (v0.3 §5.2):** The spec's R-DID MUST requirement — one new unique R-DID per relationship — materially reduces this risk for compliant implementations. However, the M-DID bootstrapping exception (Privacy Considerations §9) creates a residual window: if migration to R-DIDs is never triggered normatively, early-phase M-DID usage remains linkable.
risk.harm_description: Member's full community participation graph exposed; surveillance by state actors; chilling effect on membership in politically sensitive VTCs.

risk.name: Over-Disclosure in IDVC Schema
risk.description: The IDVC schema requires or permits more personal data than strictly necessary. Excess data increases breach impact and enables cross-system correlation.
risk.harm_description: Excessive personal data collected; breach exposes more than necessary; correlation with external databases enables de-anonymisation.

risk.name: Credential Schema Ambiguity
risk.description: Underspecified VRC, VMC, or IDVC schemas lead to inconsistent implementation across personal network managers, VTAs, and IDVPs — creating interoperability failures and policy bypass opportunities. **SPEC UPDATE (v0.3 §2–§4):** The spec defines a formal W3C VC type hierarchy and normative base structure (§4), reducing schema ambiguity for the six DTG credential types. However, the DTG JSON-LD context (`firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1`) is not yet published as a resolvable normative artefact, and no conformance test suite exists. Schema ambiguity risk is partially reduced but not resolved.
risk.harm_description: VTA rejects valid credentials due to schema mismatch; non-compliant implementations admit members who should be rejected; community trust damaged.

risk.name: Personal Network Manager UX Failure
risk.description: The personal network manager presents cryptographic operations incomprehensibly to non-technical members, causing errors, abandonment, or security failures. The DTGWG itself acknowledges UX as 'the single hardest problem'.
risk.harm_description: Members generate unsafe keys; incorrect M-DID selection creates linkability; members abandon onboarding; trust task ceremonies not completed correctly.

risk.name: Key Loss / Recovery Failure
risk.description: A member loses access to their M-DID private key with no recovery mechanism, rendering their membership credential unverifiable and participation irrecoverable.
risk.harm_description: Member locked out permanently; trust graph has orphaned nodes; key recovery attempts create identity fraud risk if not properly gated.

risk.name: Credential Revocation Without Due Process
risk.description: A VMC is revoked without prior notice, documented rationale, or accessible appeals. May be triggered by anchor pressure, administrative error, or deliberate abuse.
risk.harm_description: Member unjustly excluded; professional or reputational harm; no remedy available; chilling effect on participation for other members.

risk.name: Stale Credential / Expiry Without Renewal Path
risk.description: VTC credentials expire without a clear, accessible renewal pathway. Members unable to renew lose membership inadvertently.
risk.harm_description: Active members locked out through administrative failure; valuable contributors excluded; trust in credential infrastructure eroded.

risk.name: Revocation Cascade / Cross-VTC Contamination
risk.description: Revocation in one VTC propagates to credentials in other unrelated VTCs, or revocation status becomes globally visible.
risk.harm_description: Member penalised across multiple communities for a single community's decision; effective blacklisting without cross-community due process.

risk.name: ZKP Implementation Failure
risk.description: Zero-knowledge proof implementations for privacy-preserving IDVC presentation or revocation are incorrectly implemented, introducing soundness or zero-knowledge property failures.
risk.harm_description: Member identity data exposed despite expectation of privacy; forged ZKP proofs used to pass admission checks with invalid credentials.

risk.name: Quantum / Algorithm Obsolescence
risk.description: Cryptographic algorithms underpinning VTC credentials become vulnerable to quantum computing attacks or are deprecated, requiring coordinated migration of all community credentials. **SPEC UPDATE (v0.3 §9):** The spec's format-agnostic ZKP design — explicitly not binding to BBS+, SD-JWT-VC, or any specific scheme — reduces algorithm lock-in and partially supports algorithm agility (CT-29). The spec does not yet define a migration pathway or post-quantum readiness assessment requirement.
risk.harm_description: All existing credentials become cryptographically untrustworthy; mass re-issuance required; members without updated tooling excluded during transition.

risk.name: Agent Credential Scope Creep
risk.description: An AI agent exceeds the cryptographic capability constraints in its delegation credential through misconfiguration, vulnerability, or adversarial prompt injection.
risk.harm_description: Agent performs unauthorised credential operations; if compromised, attacker gains persistent trusted access with full operator permissions.

risk.name: Stale Agent After Operator Revocation
risk.description: An AI agent continues to operate and present credentials after its human operator's VMC has been revoked, because revocation does not propagate to the agent credential.
risk.harm_description: Revoked member's agent maintains unauthorised VTC access; governance decisions may be influenced by a member no longer legitimate.

risk.name: AI-Mediated Sybil Generation at Scale
risk.description: A malicious actor deploys AI agents to automate synthetic identity creation and coordinated VRC vouching at a speed that overwhelms human review capacity and defeats standard rate-limiting.
risk.harm_description: VTC trust graph flooded with synthetic members; governance capture by AI-controlled fake identities; admission controls rendered ineffective.

risk.name: LLM-Powered Social Engineering of Anchors
risk.description: Adversarial AI agents generate convincing synthetic communications to social-engineer community trust anchors into issuing VRCs or invitation credentials to fraudulent applicants. **SPEC UPDATE (v0.3 §7.3):** The Witness Credential (VWC) provides a partial technical counter-measure: requiring a VWC from a trusted in-person or out-of-band witness for high-stakes anchor-level VRCs makes AI-generated synthetic personas harder to sustain. This does not eliminate the risk but raises the operational cost of the attack.
risk.harm_description: Fraudulent members admitted through compromised anchor vouching; anchor reputation and liability implicated; trust graph integrity undermined.

risk.name: State-Level Coercion of Anchors / IDVPs
risk.description: A government agency legally compels trust anchors, IDVPs, or registry operators to disclose member identities, revoke credentials for political purposes, or grant unauthorised write access.
risk.harm_description: Dissidents identified and targeted via VTC membership data; members forced out under political pressure; VTC becomes instrument of state surveillance.

risk.name: Registry Censorship / Denial of Service
risk.description: A state actor or adversary blocks access to the VTC trust registry or VTA, preventing credential verification and collapsing VTC operations.
risk.harm_description: VTC operations halted; members unable to verify credentials or be admitted; VTA unavailability cascades to relying parties.

risk.name: Legal / Regulatory Framework Conflict
risk.description: VTC operations or credential schemes conflict with applicable data protection law (GDPR, eIDAS 2.0) or national identity law, exposing the governing body to liability.
risk.harm_description: Governing body exposed to regulatory fines; members' data processed unlawfully; IDVP faces licence revocation; VTC forced to suspend operations.

risk.name: Chilling Effect on Community Participation
risk.description: Members self-censor or reduce participation because VTC membership, credential graph, or communications are observable by governance bodies or adversaries.
risk.harm_description: Community loses diversity and candour; whistle-blowers and dissidents avoid participation; community loses the genuine peer relationship value that DTG is designed to enable.

risk.name: Discriminatory Vouching Practices
risk.description: Trust anchors or members informally apply discriminatory criteria when vouching, perpetuating social biases even when formal admission criteria are non-discriminatory.
risk.harm_description: Marginalised groups excluded through informal practices; VTC replicates existing social inequalities; legal exposure for governing body.

risk.name: Reputational Harm from Public Revocation
risk.description: A member's revocation status is disclosed publicly in a way that damages their professional or personal reputation, even if the revocation was erroneous or later overturned.
risk.harm_description: Member suffers professional consequences before appeal is resolved; reputational harm not remedied even if appeal succeeds; chilling effect on participation for others.

risk.name: Trust Graph Capture by Coordinated Actor
risk.description: A coordinated adversary — through Sybil attacks, anchor collusion, or gradual infiltration — gains sufficient influence to control admission decisions, governance votes, or community norms.
risk.harm_description: VTC governance captured by malicious actors; legitimate members outvoted or silenced; community used as infrastructure for further attacks; DTG ecosystem integrity undermined.

risk.name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behaviour (CIB) in Governance
risk.description: A coordinated disinformation network exploits governance mechanisms to undermine anchor reputations, exhaust governance bandwidth, and fragment community consensus.
risk.harm_description: Trust anchors resign or make poor decisions under attack; governance bandwidth consumed; VTC unable to function as intended.

risk.name: Open Issues Left Unresolved at Scale
risk.description: The four open issues in the VTC Bootstrapping Draft — uniqueness, trust task protocols, expiration/revocation, DID document storage — remain unresolved when the VTC scales beyond small community management.
risk.harm_description: Uniqueness enforcement fails at scale; revocation mechanisms fail under load; DID documents become irresolvable; trust task protocols incompatible across implementations.

risk.name: VRC Over-Disclosure — Rich Data in Core Edge
risk.description: The VRC schema (spec §5.2) requires only the target DID and proof, but places no constraint on what additional data may be embedded in `credentialSubject`. Implementers who embed rich relationship metadata — relationship duration, first-meeting location, mutual endorsements — directly in VRCs rather than using the annotation credential layer (VPC, VEC, VWC) create credentials in which both parties have cryptographically committed to that data. It cannot then be selectively disclosed or withheld from verifiers. The annotation credential architecture exists in the spec but is not normatively required as the channel for supplementary data. **Introduced by:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 analysis (RAHP commentary §2.4).
risk.harm_description: Members inadvertently commit to more personal data than intended in bilateral VRCs; ZKP selective disclosure is undermined because the data is in the core credential, not an annotation; relationship graphs become richer surveillance targets than necessary.

risk.name: M-DID Bootstrapping Exception Undermines R-DID Privacy
risk.description: Spec §5.2 permits M-DIDs 'for bootstrapping' with no normative migration trigger or timeline. The Privacy Considerations section (§9) recommends migration to R-DIDs post-bootstrapping but does not make this a normative requirement. In practice, if migration never happens — the likely outcome without a phase-gate — early VRC relationships remain M-DID-based. An adversary monitoring the trust registry during the bootstrapping phase can reconstruct membership graphs from M-DID co-occurrences in VRCs issued before migration. **Introduced by:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §5.2 and Privacy Considerations §9 (RAHP commentary §2.5).
risk.harm_description: The R-DID architecture's privacy guarantee is contingent on migration actually happening. Without a normative trigger, the bootstrapping exception becomes the permanent operating mode for many implementations. State actors and registry observers can reconstruct trust graphs from the pre-migration VRC corpus.

risk.name: Endorsement Credential (VEC) Manipulation
risk.description: Spec §7.2 defines the VEC's `endorsement` field as 'community/VTN-defined — structure and fields determined by community policy.' This maximum flexibility, with no normative constraint requiring endorsers to be co-members of the same VTC as the endorsed party, creates a reputation manipulation attack surface. A coordinated bad-faith actor can issue large volumes of fabricated VECs with high `competencyLevel` claims to inflate the reputation of synthetic personas, then use those reputational signals to gain governance influence. **Introduced by:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §7.2 (RAHP commentary §2.8).
risk.harm_description: Synthetic personas receive artificially inflated reputation scores via coordinated VEC issuance; governance decisions influenced by reputational signals that are manufactured rather than earned; admission thresholds gamed via endorsement proxies.

risk.name: Governanceless VTC Claiming Credential Compliance
risk.description: The DTG Credential Specification v0.3 defines credential schemas (§2–§8) and normative credential requirements without requiring that a VTC deploying these credentials has any governance framework in place. A developer group could deploy technically compliant VMCs and VRCs — passing all credential-layer verification checks — while operating with no genesis policy, no time-bounded initiator authority, and no trust anchor diversity requirements. Relying parties would have no normative signal that governance is absent. **Introduced by:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 analysis — gap identified in §9 (Trust Registries section) and commentary §2.9.
risk.harm_description: Relying parties accept VMCs from VTCs with no governance backing; DTG compliance signals trustworthiness that does not exist at the governance layer; a single actor controls a 'compliant' VTC indefinitely with no accountability.

risk.name: Incapacity / Unsupported Decision-Making Exclusion
risk.description: The VTC admission and ongoing participation architecture assumes all members are adults with full independent legal capacity. Persons who require supported decision-making — including minors with SEN (EC1), adults with progressive cognitive impairment (EC2a), and others acting under delegated authority — are structurally excluded or forced into non-compliant workarounds. The credential architecture has no concept of co-signed or supported consent distinct from substituted decision-making.
risk.harm_description: Persons requiring support are excluded from VTC participation entirely, or their participation is mediated through impersonation-equivalent workarounds (a guardian using their own DID on behalf of the member). Admission denials fall disproportionately on disabled people, older adults with declining capacity, and minors — groups with legal protection against discrimination. Governance decisions affecting these members lack due process adapted to their situation.

risk.name: Legal Capacity Architecture Gap — LPA / Guardianship Not Representable
risk.description: A registered Lasting Power of Attorney (or equivalent legal guardianship instrument) has no representation in the DTG credential architecture. The VTC system cannot distinguish a legitimate LPA holder authenticating on behalf of a donor from an account takeover. Governance communications (revocation notices, renewal reminders, appeals deadlines) are addressed to the credential holder's contact details — which an incapacitated person cannot access — with no secondary recipient mechanism. The LPA holder has no audit-trail separate from the donor, and no defined pathway to close an M-DID on the donor's death.
risk.harm_description: A person who has lost capacity loses their VTC membership by default because no one can operate their credentials lawfully. Legitimate LPA holders are treated as unauthorised actors. Revocation due process rights (GR-08) are forfeited because notices reach an inaccessible account. The governing body cannot involve the LPA holder in governance processes. On death, the M-DID is abandoned rather than formally closed, leaving a ghost node in the trust graph and no tamper-evident record of the credential lifecycle end.

risk.name: Credential Lifecycle Abandonment on Capacity Loss or Death
risk.description: When a member loses capacity progressively (e.g., dementia) or dies, the DTG architecture has no defined lifecycle event for credential closure, dormancy, or attorney-mediated continuation. The M-DID simply goes silent. There is no mechanism for the trust graph to record a capacity transition, for credentials to enter an attorney-managed state, or for a death notification to propagate to relying parties. The spec addresses revocation but not the end of life as a credential lifecycle event.
risk.harm_description: Ghost nodes accumulate in the trust graph: members who have lost capacity or died appear as active participants. Trust graph topology calculations (anchor diversity, reciprocity rates) are distorted by stale nodes. Relying parties may accept credentials from a deceased member's DID. Family members or attorneys have no recognised pathway to close the account, creating distress and potential identity misuse risk. The absence of a death-closure pathway also means a malicious actor could continue operating a deceased member's DID without detection.

risk.name: Minor Data Exposure via Co-Signatory Inference
risk.description: When a minor (or person lacking full independent capacity) applies to join a VTC, any co-signatory structure in the admission credential implicitly signals that the credential holder has reduced or delegated capacity. This disclosure is not consented to: the minor's SEN status, age, or disability is inferred from the governance structure itself, even if no explicit SEN attribute is included in the credential. The UK Online Safety Act 2023 and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 impose additional obligations on systems processing children's data, which a VTC admitting under-18s becomes subject to — often without realising it.
risk.harm_description: A minor's SEN profile, disability status, or reduced capacity is disclosed without their consent to any party that can observe the credential structure. This constitutes processing of special-category data under UK GDPR without a lawful basis. The VTC governing body becomes subject to Online Safety Act 2023 children's data obligations without necessarily having the governance structures to comply. Failure to protect this inferred data creates regulatory exposure and reputational harm to the minor.

risk.name: Child Safety Non-Compliance — Age Assurance Failure
risk.description: A minor successfully obtains or presents a valid-appearing over-18 IDVC, whether through IDVP failure, synthetic credential generation by Phantom (M2) or Viktor (B1), a ZKP implementation gap (RK-CY01), or an architecture flaw in the age assurance pathway. This is a non-negotiable child safety failure with criminal liability implications under the Online Safety Act 2023 for any age-restricted relying party (e.g., EC4 Velvet Gate). Unlike other register risks, this risk has a binary outcome: any non-zero incident rate is a system-level failure. The Ofcom regime provides no safe harbour for technical failure where the architecture was knowingly immature.
risk.harm_description: A minor accesses age-restricted content due to a false-positive age assurance outcome. The relying party faces Ofcom enforcement action including fines up to £18 million or 10% of global qualifying revenue. Criminal liability for platform operators is possible under OSA 2023. The IDVP that issued the compromised credential faces deregistration and regulatory action. The DTG architecture's fitness for age-assurance use cases is brought into question, with potential for wider loss of trust in the ecosystem. The harm to the child is primary and irreversible.

risk.name: Organisational Identity Architecture Gap
risk.description: The DTG Credential Specification v0.3 defines credential schemas for individual natural persons. An NHS Foundation Trust (EC3) or other regulated organisation seeking to participate as a VTC member holds institutional identity, makes decisions through board governance rather than individual consent, and has complex internal authority chains (Caldicott Guardian, CDO, board resolution) that cannot be represented in the current C-DID model. Regulatory compliance (NHS DSPT, DCB3051, CQC) requires the organisation's governance to be traceable to its credential operations in ways the current architecture does not support. The DTG spec has no organisational credential type.
risk.harm_description: Regulated organisations cannot participate in the DTG ecosystem in a compliant way. NHS Trusts cannot issue VMCs interoperable with the NHS Digital Staff Passport. The absence of an organisational identity model means the DTG ecosystem remains limited to individual participants, excluding the institutional sector that would drive adoption at scale. Organisations that attempt to participate using workarounds (an individual holding a C-DID on behalf of an institution) create unrecognised personal liability and governance gaps.

risk.name: IDVP Regulatory Cascade — Cross-Jurisdiction Age Assurance
risk.description: An age-restricted relying party (EC4) relies on IDVCs issued by IDVPs registered in the VTC trust registry. Where subscribers are located internationally, their IDVCs may have been issued by IDVPs whose trust registry standing is uncertain, whose jurisdiction's age verification standards differ from UK Ofcom requirements, or who have subsequently been deregistered or compromised (cf. RK-ID03, AU10TIX breach 2024). The relying party cannot independently verify the current standing of a foreign IDVP in near-real-time without a cross-jurisdiction trust registry resolution mechanism. The Online Safety Act 2023 does not provide a safe harbour for good-faith reliance on a deregistered IDVP.
risk.harm_description: A relying party accepts an IDVC from a subscriber whose IDVP has been deregistered or was never compliant with UK Ofcom standards. Ofcom finds the age assurance technically inadequate regardless of the relying party's good faith. The relying party faces enforcement action. The DTG trust registry does not have a defined mechanism for propagating IDVP deregistration to relying parties in near-real-time across jurisdictions. The broader IDVP ecosystem loses confidence in the DTG trust registry as a reliable source of IDVP standing.

risk.name: Credential Schema Gap — Supported Consent and LPA Not Representable
risk.description: The current VRC, VMC, and IDVC schemas assume a single credential holder who is the same legal person as the consent-giver, the DID controller, and the community participant. The schemas have no field or structure for: (a) co-signed admission where the signatory is not a substituted decision-maker; (b) a delegation credential representing a registered LPA; (c) a capacity-status flag indicating that the holder currently operates under supported or substituted decision-making; or (d) a secondary notification recipient registered in the trust registry. These gaps mean the architecture literally cannot represent legal relationships that exist in the real world for an estimated 1.3 million people in England and Wales alone (LPA registrations as of 2025).
risk.harm_description: The credential architecture cannot serve a large class of legitimate participants without introducing impersonation-equivalent workarounds. Any attempt to accommodate these users without schema changes creates governance ambiguity, audit trail corruption (Margaret's actions appear as Arthur's), and potential violations of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 (which requires clear records of attorney decision-making). Standards bodies that adopt the DTG spec without addressing this gap will produce a credential ecosystem that is legally non-compliant in the UK, EU, and any jurisdiction with equivalent incapacity law.

control.name: Version-Controlled Public Genesis Policy
control.description: All Phase 1 bootstrapping policies must be committed to a public, version-controlled record before Phase 2 begins. This creates an auditable baseline for community governance.

control.name: Independent Governance Review at Genesis
control.description: An independent review of bootstrap policies by parties other than the initiator must be completed before the VTC admits non-initiator members. Reviewer identity and findings to be recorded.

control.name: Governance Transition Milestones
control.description: Explicit milestones for transitioning initiator authority to the governing body must be defined and documented before Phase 2. The VTA PEP enforces authority expiry at the documented milestone.

control.name: Trust Anchor Diversity Policy
control.description: A minimum diversity standard for trust anchors — geographic, organisational, cultural — must be defined and enforced before Phase 2 seeding. Homogeneous anchor clusters constitute a policy violation.

control.name: Anchor Clustering Metric Monitoring
control.description: The VTA tracks an anchor clustering metric (e.g. organisational or jurisdictional Herfindahl index). Breaches of the diversity floor trigger a governance alert before additional anchors are admitted.

control.name: Governance Capacity Planning
control.description: The governing body must conduct annual capacity planning for admission, appeals, revocation, and security incident workloads, including adversarial load scenarios.

control.name: Complaint / Appeals Rate-Limiting
control.description: The VTA or governance portal enforces rate-limiting on complaint and appeal submissions per member per time period, without suppressing legitimate single-member grievances.

control.name: Uniqueness Enforcement Mechanism
control.description: A documented uniqueness enforcement mechanism must be in place before Phase 4 opens. Acceptable approaches include ZKP personhood proofs, trusted IDVP attestation, or social recovery quorum. Absence must be formally risk-accepted.

control.name: Vouching Pattern Anomaly Detection
control.description: The VTA or a monitoring layer analyses vouching patterns for statistical anomalies — e.g. tight clusters of mutual vouching from a small group — and triggers governance review when thresholds are breached.

control.name: Non-Discriminatory Admission Criteria
control.description: Admission criteria must be published, non-discriminatory, and reviewed against applicable equality law before Phase 3 opens. Criteria must not create de facto barriers for specific cultural, geographic, or socioeconomic groups.

control.name: Alternative Identity Proofing Paths
control.description: At least one admission pathway must not require conventional government-issued ID, to accommodate the estimated 850 million people globally who lack recognised ID documents. Alternative proofing options must be documented in governance.

control.name: IDVP Security Approval Criteria
control.description: IDVPs must meet documented security and operational standards — including breach notification obligations — before being approved and registered in the VTC trust registry.

control.name: IDVP Deregistration Handling Protocol
control.description: The governing body must define how member VMCs issued via a deregistered IDVP's IDVCs are handled: whether they remain valid, require re-verification, or are revoked. The protocol must include member notification within an agreed SLA.

control.name: DID Document Integrity Verification
control.description: The VTA must verify DID document integrity cryptographically before accepting any credential presentation, using tamper-evident registry entries or equivalent mechanism. DID document storage and access requirements must be specified in the credential spec.

control.name: Pseudonymous Per-VTC M-DID Design
control.description: Personal network managers should generate a distinct M-DID per VTC, and registry metadata exposure should be minimised to prevent cross-community profiling. This should be a normative design requirement in the DTG credential specification.

control.name: Minimum-Necessary IDVC Attribute Set
control.description: A defined minimum-necessary IDVC attribute set must be published before Phase 4, specifying only attributes strictly required by VTC admission policy. DPIA must be completed before IDVC schema is deployed.

control.name: Data Minimisation Audit
control.description: An annual data minimisation audit of all credential schemas (VRC, VMC, IDVC) must be conducted to identify and remove attributes no longer required by policy.

control.name: Normative Credential Schema Publication
control.description: Normative credential schemas for VRC, VMC, and IDVC must be published before Phase 2. Schemas must include version identifiers and a backwards-compatibility policy.

control.name: Conformance Test Suite
control.description: A conformance test suite for VTA and personal network manager implementations must be published, enabling automated verification that implementations correctly enforce admission policies and credential schemas.

control.name: Sovereign Wallet UX Design Principles
control.description: UX design principles for sovereign wallets must be defined, addressing task-based trust ceremonies, plain-language guidance, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA minimum), and user testing with non-technical participants before launch.

control.name: Non-Technical User Onboarding Testing
control.description: Structured user testing with non-technical participants must be conducted before each major release of the personal network manager, covering the Phase 1–4 trust task ceremonies.

control.name: Key Recovery Mechanism
control.description: A key recovery mechanism — e.g. social recovery quorum, hardware backup — must be defined and documented in the personal network manager UX. Governance policy for M-DID replacement must cover recovery scenarios.

control.name: Mandatory Pre-Revocation Notice
control.description: No VMC shall be revoked without prior written notice to the member, including documented rationale and the available appeals pathway, delivered within an agreed notice period (recommended: minimum 14 days except emergency security revocations).

control.name: Privacy-Preserving Revocation Disclosure
control.description: Revocation status must not be publicly linked to a member's real-world identity by default. ZKP-based status lists (e.g. W3C Status List 2021 with ZKP) or equivalent privacy-preserving mechanisms should be used.

control.name: Credential Renewal Workflow
control.description: A defined credential renewal workflow — including advance expiry notification (recommended: 30 days) and a grace period — must be implemented before Phase 4. Autonomous agent renewal (US-08) addresses this for agent-managed credentials.

control.name: VTC-Scoped Revocation
control.description: Revocation must be explicitly scoped to the issuing VTC only. Cross-VTC revocation requires a separate, documented governance decision by each affected VTC's governing body.

control.name: Audited ZKP Library Requirement
control.description: Only ZKP implementations that have undergone formal security review or are from audited open-source libraries may be used in VTC credential workflows. The DTGWG charter identifies ZKP as a major focus area.

control.name: ZKP Conformance Testing
control.description: A conformance test suite for ZKP implementations must be developed as part of the DTG credential specification, covering soundness, completeness, and zero-knowledge properties.

control.name: Algorithm Agility and Migration Pathway
control.description: VTC credential schemas must be designed for algorithm agility. A quantum-readiness assessment and migration pathway must be defined in governance and reviewed at least every two years.

control.name: Cryptographic Delegation Scope Constraints
control.description: AI agent delegation credentials must cryptographically encode explicit capability constraints (e.g. permitted credential types, target VTCs, time window). The VTA PEP must enforce these constraints and reject out-of-scope operations.

control.name: Short-Lived Agent Credentials
control.description: AI agent delegation credentials should be short-lived (recommended: maximum 24-hour validity) with automated renewal tied to operator membership liveness checks, reducing the window of exposure for compromised agent credentials.

control.name: Agent Liveness Check on Operator VMC
control.description: Before executing any delegated credential operation, an AI agent must verify that its operator's VMC remains valid in the VTC trust registry. Operator revocation must propagate to agent credential invalidation within an agreed SLA (recommended: ≤1 hour).

control.name: Non-Human Activity Rate-Limiting
control.description: The VTA and governance portal must enforce rate-limiting on admission requests, credential presentations, and invitation submissions, calibrated to distinguish human from automated activity patterns.

control.name: Behavioural Anomaly Detection for Non-Human Actors
control.description: A behavioural anomaly detection layer must be deployed before Phase 4 to identify non-human activity patterns, including high-frequency admission attempts, coordinated vouching, and adversarial policy fuzzing.

control.name: Anchor Awareness of AI Social Engineering
control.description: Community trust anchors must receive training on AI-powered social engineering vectors, including LLM-generated synthetic personas. Training must be updated at least annually.

control.name: Out-of-Band Verification for High-Stakes Vouching
control.description: For Phase 2 trust anchor admission and Phase 3 high-trust vouching, anchors should use out-of-band verification (e.g. video call, in-person meeting) before issuing VRCs, particularly when requests arrive via digital-only channels.

control.name: Jurisdictional Diversity of Key Parties
control.description: The governing body must document the jurisdictional distribution of trust anchors and IDVPs, and assess the risk of any single jurisdiction having coercive legal leverage over a controlling majority of key parties.

control.name: Legal Coercion Response Protocol
control.description: A documented legal coercion response protocol must be in place for trust anchors and IDVPs, including guidance on legal rights, obligations, escalation contacts, and member notification procedures when disclosure orders are received.

control.name: Distributed Registry Architecture
control.description: The VTC trust registry must be deployed with geographic redundancy and a defined degraded-mode operation specification, so that VTA unavailability in one region does not collapse VTC operations globally.

control.name: Legal Review of Credential Schemas
control.description: A legal review of all credential schemas and trust registry designs against applicable data protection law (GDPR, eIDAS 2.0) must be completed before Phase 4. A DPO (or equivalent) must sign off on IDVC processing.

control.name: Open Issues Regulatory Risk Acceptance
control.description: Each of the four VTC Bootstrapping Draft open issues must have an explicit regulatory risk assessment, and any accepted risks must be formally signed by the governing body with a review date.

control.name: Anonymous Membership Option
control.description: For VTCs operating in politically sensitive contexts, an anonymous membership pathway — using ZKP proofs of valid credentials without linking to real-world identity — should be available.

control.name: Governing Body Accountability for Systematic Exclusion
control.description: The governing body must track admission denial rates by demographic proxy where legally permissible, and must have a defined escalation process when systematic exclusion patterns are identified.

control.name: Remediation Pathway After Overturned Revocation
control.description: Where a revocation is overturned on appeal, a documented remediation pathway must exist, including restoration of credentials, notification to relevant parties, and record correction.

control.name: Multi-Party Registry Write Authorisation
control.description: Trust registry writes must require multi-party or threshold authorisation (e.g. m-of-n signature). No single actor — including an IDVP, anchor, or registry operator — shall have unilateral write access. All writes must be logged in a tamper-evident audit trail.

control.name: Coordinated Behaviour Detection in Governance
control.description: The complaints and appeals workflow must include coordinated behaviour detection, identifying statistically anomalous submission patterns (timing, content similarity, source clustering) that indicate organised bad-faith campaigns.

control.name: Formal Open Issues Mitigation Plan
control.description: Each of the four VTC Bootstrapping Draft open issues must have a formal mitigation plan with owner, target resolution date, and interim risk controls, signed by the governing body before Phase 4.

control.name: Threat Model Maintenance
control.description: A formal VTC threat model must be published, reviewed, and updated at least annually. It must cover at minimum: Sybil attacks, state coercion, anchor collusion, AI-mediated attacks, registry manipulation, and CIB in governance.

control.name: VRC Data Minimisation Clause
control.description: The VRC `credentialSubject` SHOULD contain only the minimum claims necessary for graph structure: the target party's DID and the `validFrom` timestamp. Additional relationship metadata (skills, event context, endorsements) SHOULD be expressed through annotation credentials (VPC, VEC, VWC per spec §7) rather than embedded in the VRC itself. Implementations MUST NOT require VRC subjects to include personal data beyond that strictly required by VTC admission policy. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 commentary recommendation R6 (§2.4).

control.name: M-DID to R-DID Migration Trigger
control.description: VTC implementations MUST define and publish a normative trigger for migration from M-DID-based to R-DID-based VRC edges, as required by spec §5.2 privacy intent. The trigger SHOULD occur before Phase 4 opens or before the VTC exceeds a governance-defined membership threshold. After the trigger, new VRCs MUST use R-DIDs. The migration trigger condition and date MUST be recorded in the trust registry. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §5.2 Privacy Considerations and commentary recommendation R7 (§2.5).

control.name: Non-Human DID Designation in DID Document
control.description: Agent DIDs MUST be designated as non-human in the DID Document using a defined service type property or a `@type` assertion, enabling VTAs to apply agent-specific policy. VTAs MAY reject VMC applications from DIDs not carrying a human attestation where VTC policy requires proof of personhood. This creates a normative distinction between Aether (M1) and Phantom (M2) at the DID layer. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 analysis — gap in §5.1/§5.2 (commentary §2.3, recommendation R1, §10.1).

control.name: Agent Delegation Credential Requirement
control.description: An AI agent operating on behalf of a human VTC member MUST hold a delegation credential issued by that member's M-DID, referencing the member's VMC and specifying the agent's permitted capability scope as a normative `credentialSubject` claim. Without this, the spec's VMC schema cannot distinguish an authorised agent (Aether, M1) from an adversarial one (Phantom, M2). **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 analysis — gap in §5.1 (commentary §2.3, recommendation R1, §10.2).

control.name: VIC Role Embedding (membershipRole field)
control.description: The VIC `credentialSubject` SHOULD include a `membershipRole` field specifying the role to be granted upon admission (e.g. 'trustAnchor', 'member'). This allows the issuer to cryptographically commit to the intended role at invitation time, enabling offline verification and making the VIC tamper-evident with respect to role assignment — independent of trust registry availability. The spec's open question ('Q: Should any of this be embedded in the VIC?') in §6.1 should be resolved in this direction. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §6.1 open question (commentary recommendation R4, §2.6).

control.name: VWC Requirement for High-Stakes Anchor Admission
control.description: For Phase 2 trust anchor admission, VTC governance SHOULD require that VRCs used in anchor admission packages be accompanied by a Witness Credential (VWC per spec §7.3) from a trusted third party attesting to the in-person or verified out-of-band nature of the relationship. This directly implements CT-36 (Out-of-Band Verification) using the VWC schema and raises the cost of AI-generated synthetic anchor persona attacks (RK-AI04). The VWC `witnessContext.method` field should record the verification method. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §7.3 (commentary §1.4, recommendation R9).

control.name: VEC Issuer Co-Membership Requirement
control.description: VTC implementations SHOULD require that Endorsement Credential (VEC per spec §7.2) issuers hold a valid VMC from the same C-DID as the endorsed party. VTA policy enforcement points SHOULD verify this co-membership before treating VEC-based reputation signals as valid inputs to admission or governance decisions. Aggregated VEC metrics SHOULD be treated with appropriate scepticism where endorsements form tight clusters from a small issuer group. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §7.2 — underspecification identified in commentary §2.8, recommendation R10.

control.name: VTC Governance Conformance Class
control.description: A VTC claiming DTG credential specification compliance MUST publish a version-controlled governance framework satisfying the requirements of the DTG VTC Governance Specification (forthcoming). At minimum this must include: a genesis policy record (GR-01), a time-bounded initiator authority mechanism (GR-02), and a trust anchor diversity policy (GR-03). The trust registry entry for a DTG-compliant VTC SHOULD include a resolvable reference to its published governance framework. Without this, technical credential compliance provides false assurance to relying parties. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §9 (Trust Registries) — gap identified in commentary §2.9, recommendation R8.

control.name: Supported Decision-Making Credential Extension
control.description: Extend the VRC and VMC schema with an optional co-signatory field that distinguishes supported consent (co-signatory assists but member retains decision authority) from substituted consent (attorney acts in place of member). The distinction must be cryptographically attestable and auditable separately from the core credential.
control.rationale: Required to represent legally recognised supported decision-making without creating impersonation-equivalent workarounds.

control.name: Accessible Trust Task Ceremony UX for Cognitive Differences
control.description: Trust task ceremony implementations must offer accessibility profiles adapted for users with executive function differences (autism spectrum, ADHD, acquired cognitive impairment). Profiles must be negotiable between parties without disclosing the reason for the adaptation request. Minimum requirements: simplified QR code flows, extended session timeouts, plain-language guidance, and support for a co-present third party during the ceremony.
control.rationale: Directly addresses ceremony completion failure for EC1 and similar users; linked to EPIC-18.

control.name: LPA Delegation Credential Type
control.description: Define a new credential type — the Legal Delegation Credential (LDC) — that represents a registered legal authority (Lasting Power of Attorney, court-appointed deputyship, or equivalent) as a scope-limited delegation relationship. The LDC must: name the attorney and donor DIDs; reference the legal instrument by registration number; constrain the attorney's authorised operations; and be registered in the VTC trust registry as a discoverable relationship distinct from ordinary member credentials.
control.rationale: Required to represent LPA in the architecture; without this, RK-HX05 cannot be mitigated.

control.name: Secondary Notification Recipient Registration
control.description: The VTC trust registry and governance communication systems must support registration of one or more secondary notification recipients for a member's credential lifecycle events (revocation notices, renewal reminders, appeals deadlines). Where an LDC is registered, the attorney named in the LDC must be automatically enrolled as a secondary recipient. Secondary recipient communications must be cryptographically authenticated and separate from the primary member account.
control.rationale: Required for GR-08 revocation due process to function where the primary holder lacks capacity.

control.name: M-DID Closure and Death Notification Pathway
control.description: Define a governed lifecycle pathway for M-DID closure upon death or permanent incapacity, including: a notification mechanism for the trust graph; a tamper-evident closure record; a portability package for the credential history; and an attorney or next-of-kin confirmation workflow. The VTC governing body must publish its M-DID closure procedure as part of its governance documentation.
control.rationale: Addresses ghost-node accumulation and missing end-of-life credential lifecycle event.

control.name: Age Assurance Compliance Verification Requirement
control.description: Any VTC that admits an age-restricted relying party (i.e., a VTC member or relying party operating under the Online Safety Act 2023 Part 5 or equivalent) must verify that: (a) the ZKP implementation used for age proofs has been independently audited; (b) the IDVP trust registry entry includes an age-verification scope claim; and (c) the relying party's Ofcom-compliant audit record template is reviewed by the VTC governing body before the relying party is admitted. The governing body must maintain documented evidence of this review.
control.rationale: Required to establish governing body accountability for child safety outcomes in age-assurance use cases.

control.name: Organisational Credential Type Definition
control.description: Define a new credential type — the Organisational Member Credential (OMC) — that represents an organisation (rather than a natural person) as a VTC participant. The OMC must: identify the organisation by legal identifier (company number, charity number, NHS ODS code, etc.); name the individual officers responsible for credential operations (with their personal DIDs); specify the internal governance process by which the organisation authorises credential actions; and bind the organisation's regulatory compliance status as an attestable claim.
control.rationale: Without an organisational credential type, the DTG ecosystem cannot accommodate regulated institutions; required for NHS and similar use cases.

control.name: Organisational Governance Conformance Mapping
control.description: For organisations seeking VTC membership, the VTC governing body must assess whether the organisation's existing internal governance framework (e.g., NHS DSPT, CQC registration, ISO 27001) satisfies the VTC governance conformance class (CT-56). Where it does, this equivalence must be formally documented and recorded in the trust registry as an attestable claim, avoiding duplication of governance processes that would be incompatible with public sector procurement timescales.
control.rationale: Required to make the DTG accessible to regulated organisations without requiring governance duplication.

control.name: Cross-Jurisdiction IDVP Standing Verification
control.description: The VTC trust registry must expose a machine-readable, near-real-time IDVP standing endpoint that age-restricted relying parties can query at the point of credential presentation. For IDVPs operating under non-UK regulatory frameworks, the registry must include a jurisdictional scope claim and a date-of-last-verification. Relying parties must not accept IDVCs from IDVPs whose registry standing cannot be confirmed at presentation time for age-assurance use cases.
control.rationale: Required for OSA 2023 compliance by age-restricted relying parties; extends existing IDVP registry standing requirement (GR-05).

control.name: Children's Data Processing Impact Assessment Requirement
control.description: Any VTC that knowingly or foreseeably admits participants under the age of 18 (including via supported decision-making pathways for minors) must complete a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) addressing children's data processing obligations under UK GDPR Article 35, the ICO Children's Code, and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. The DPIA must be completed before the first minor is admitted and reviewed annually. The VTC governing body must designate a named responsible officer for children's data compliance.
control.rationale: Required to ensure VTCs that admit minors meet statutory obligations under the UK children's data protection framework.

guardrail.name: Genesis Policy Documentation
guardrail.requirement: All Phase 1 bootstrapping policies must be version-controlled, publicly readable, and committed to an auditable record before the initiator issues any Phase 2 invitations. Hard-coded policy changes require documented governance approval.

guardrail.name: Time-Bounded Initiator Authority
guardrail.requirement: Initiator authority must be explicitly time-bounded or role-transitioned under documented governance rules. The VTA PEP must enforce the initiator count limit and refuse Phase 2 actions after authority expiry.

guardrail.name: Trust Anchor Diversity Policy
guardrail.requirement: A minimum diversity standard for trust anchors must be defined and documented before Phase 2 seeding. The VTA must enforce the anchor count limit. Homogeneous anchor clusters constitute a policy violation.

guardrail.name: Reciprocal VRC Requirement
guardrail.requirement: No VMC shall be issued to a trust anchor or member without a verified reciprocal VRC exchange. The VTA PEP must reject VMC issuance where only a unilateral VRC exists.

guardrail.name: IDVP Registry Standing
guardrail.requirement: IDVCs are only valid for VTC admission if issued by an IDVP whose DID is listed in the VTC trust registry with the role of identity verification provider at the time of presentation.

guardrail.name: Privacy-Preserving Proofing Option
guardrail.requirement: At least one privacy-preserving alternative to raw IDVC disclosure (ZKP, selective disclosure) must be available for Phase 4 admission. No applicant should be required to disclose more data than strictly necessary.

guardrail.name: Uniqueness Enforcement Mechanism
guardrail.requirement: The VTC must define and document its uniqueness enforcement mechanism before Phase 4 opens. Absence of a uniqueness mechanism at scale is an open issue and constitutes a known risk that must be risk-accepted or mitigated.

guardrail.name: Revocation Due Process
guardrail.requirement: No VMC shall be revoked without prior notice to the member, a documented rationale, and access to a formal appeals process with defined timelines. Revocation criteria must be published in the governance framework.

guardrail.name: Privacy-Preserving Revocation Disclosure
guardrail.requirement: Revocation status must not be publicly linked to member real-world identity by default. ZKP-based or status-list approaches should be used. Cross-VTC contamination must be explicitly scoped and documented.

guardrail.name: Multi-Party Registry Write Authorisation
guardrail.requirement: Trust registry writes must require multi-party or threshold authorisation. No single actor shall have unilateral write access. All registry writes must be logged in a tamper-evident audit trail.

guardrail.name: Jurisdictional Diversity for Key Parties
guardrail.requirement: The VTC governance framework must document the jurisdictional distribution of trust anchors and IDVPs, and assess the risk of any single jurisdiction having coercive legal leverage over a controlling majority of key parties.

guardrail.name: Agent Delegation Scope Constraint
guardrail.requirement: AI agents operating on behalf of VTC members must hold cryptographically scoped delegation credentials with explicit capability constraints. Operator revocation of a VMC must propagate to agent credential invalidation within an agreed latency SLA.

guardrail.name: Agent Audit Logging
guardrail.requirement: All credential operations performed by an AI agent must be logged with sufficient detail to distinguish them from human operations, including agent DID, delegation credential reference, timestamp, and action type.

guardrail.name: Non-Human Actor Detection
guardrail.requirement: Rate-limiting and behavioural anomaly detection for non-human activity patterns must be in place before Phase 4 opens. Governance rules must explicitly address agent-mediated attacks.

guardrail.name: Complaint and Appeals Rate-Limiting
guardrail.requirement: The complaints and appeals process must include rate-limiting controls to prevent bad-faith flooding, without suppressing legitimate grievances. Anti-retaliation protections for legitimate complainants must be documented.

guardrail.name: Formal Threat Model Publication
guardrail.requirement: A formal VTC threat model covering Sybil attacks, state coercion, anchor collusion, AI-mediated attacks, registry manipulation, and CIB must be published and reviewed before Phase 4 opens and at least annually thereafter.

guardrail.name: Open Issues Risk Acceptance
guardrail.requirement: The four open issues from the VTC Bootstrapping Draft — uniqueness, trust task protocols, expiration/revocation, DID document storage — must each be either mitigated or formally risk-accepted by the governing body before Phase 4 opens.

guardrail.name: R-DID Migration Phase Gate
guardrail.requirement: Before Phase 4 opens (or before the VTC exceeds a governance-defined membership threshold, whichever comes first), the VTC MUST complete migration from M-DID-based to R-DID-based VRC edges, or formally risk-accept the residual linkability exposure with a documented rationale and review date. The migration trigger MUST be recorded in the trust registry. New VRCs issued after the trigger MUST use R-DIDs. This guardrail converts the spec's §5.2 privacy RECOMMENDATION ('migration recommended post-bootstrapping') into a binding phase gate, closing the residual window identified in RK-SC04. **Source:** DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §5.2 Privacy Considerations.

guardrail.name: Supported Decision-Making and Legal Delegation Pathway
guardrail.requirement: Before a VTC may admit any participant who requires supported or substituted decision-making, or any participant for whom a registered legal authority (LPA, court deputyship, or equivalent) is in place, the VTC must: (a) have defined a supported consent pathway in its admission policy; (b) have a credential mechanism capable of representing co-signed consent and LPA delegation distinctly from substituted impersonation; and (c) have registered the legal delegation in the trust registry with a scope-limited delegation credential. Absence of this pathway is a block on admission for in-scope participants.
guardrail.applies_to_phase: Phase 3–4 (pre-condition for admission of in-scope participants)

guardrail.name: Age Assurance Architecture Readiness
guardrail.requirement: Before any VTC member may operate as an age-restricted relying party under the Online Safety Act 2023 or equivalent legislation, the governing body must verify that: (a) the ZKP implementation used for over-18 proofs has been independently audited (AT-06 extended to age context); (b) the IDVP trust registry entries used for age verification include an age-verification scope claim; (c) the IDVP's cross-jurisdiction standing can be verified in near-real-time; and (d) a child safety incident response protocol has been published. Non-compliance with this guardrail means the VTC cannot support OSA 2023-regulated use cases.
guardrail.applies_to_phase: Phase 4 (pre-condition for age-restricted relying party operations)

guardrail.name: Organisational Identity Governance Mapping
guardrail.requirement: Before a regulated organisation may be admitted as a VTC member using a C-DID or Organisational Member Credential (OMC), the governing body must: (a) verify the organisation's legal identifier and regulatory standing; (b) document the mapping between the organisation's internal governance framework and the VTC governance conformance class (CT-56); (c) identify the individual officers responsible for credential operations and their personal DIDs; and (d) confirm that the organisation's data residency requirements are compatible with the VTC trust registry's architecture. Admission without this mapping is blocked.

assurance_test.pass_criterion: Genesis policy artefact exists, is version-controlled, and was committed before any Phase 2 invitation was issued
assurance_test.verification_method: Verify via audit trail timestamp comparison — automated

assurance_test.pass_criterion: VTA PEP rejects Phase 2 invitation attempts after documented initiator authority expiry
Anchor diversity metric (geographic / organisational spread) meets documented policy floor at end of Phase 2
assurance_test.verification_method: Manual governance audit + VTA metric report

assurance_test.pass_criterion: VMC issuance fails when only one-directional VRC exists
IDVP DID not in trust registry with correct role → VTA rejects IDVC presentation
At least one ZKP / selective disclosure path is available and functional in Phase 4 UX
assurance_test.verification_method: End-to-end flow test + UX accessibility review

assurance_test.pass_criterion: Uniqueness enforcement mechanism is documented; if none exists, risk acceptance is signed and dated
Revocation notice delivered to member within SLA; appeals path accessible within 24 hours
Default revocation status disclosure does not expose member real-world identity
Registry write with single-party authorisation rejected
Jurisdictional distribution of key parties documented; coercion risk assessment signed by governing body
Agent exceeding capability constraints rejected by VTA PEP; operator VMC revocation propagates to agent within SLA
Agent credential operations visible in operator audit log with all required fields
Rate-limiting triggers on high-frequency non-human credential presentation; legitimate agent traffic not false-positively blocked
Complaint rate-limiting active; legitimate single-member complaint receives response within SLA
Published threat model exists, is dated within 12 months, and covers all six listed threat categories
All four open issues have documented mitigations or risk acceptances signed by governing body with review dates

VTC trust registry records a migration trigger date for R-DID adoption; all VRCs issued after that date use R-DIDs (not M-DIDs); OR a formal risk acceptance document is signed by the governing body with rationale and review date, committed to the version-controlled governance record before Phase 4 opens
assurance_test.verification_method: Governance audit of trust registry migration flag + sample VRC inspection
assurance_test.notes: Source: DTG Credential Spec v0.3 §5.2 Privacy Considerations

assurance_test.pass_criterion: For any VTC that has admitted or intends to admit participants under supported or substituted decision-making: (1) a supported consent pathway exists and is documented in the admission policy; (2) at least one credential mechanism can represent co-signed consent distinct from full substituted consent; (3) at least one LPA delegation credential type is registered and testable; (4) a secondary notification recipient mechanism is operational
assurance_test.verification_method: Policy review + technical test: attempt admission of a test participant with co-signatory flag; verify notification routing to secondary recipient
assurance_test.notes: Failure mode: admission either succeeds without co-signatory distinction (conflation risk) or blocks entirely (exclusion risk). Both are failures.

assurance_test.pass_criterion: For any VTC supporting an age-restricted relying party: (1) ZKP age-proof implementation has a dated independent audit report; (2) all IDVP trust registry entries used for age verification carry an age-verification scope claim; (3) IDVP standing can be queried in near-real-time at credential presentation time; (4) a published child safety incident response protocol exists naming the responsible officer
assurance_test.verification_method: Audit report review + automated test: present a ZKP over-18 proof with a deregistered IDVP DID and verify rejection; verify audit log generated
assurance_test.notes: Any failure in (4) is a non-negotiable block on age-restricted operations regardless of technical test results. Child safety non-compliance incident rate must be zero.

assurance_test.pass_criterion: For any regulated organisation admitted as a VTC member: (1) legal identifier and regulatory standing are verified against a primary source (Companies House, NHS ODS, charity register, etc.); (2) governance conformance mapping document exists and is signed by the named responsible officer; (3) individual officer DIDs are registered and linked to the organisational credential; (4) data residency compatibility is documented
assurance_test.verification_method: Document review: governance conformance mapping signed by CDO or equivalent; automated test: verify organisational credential contains legal identifier and officer DID references
assurance_test.notes: NHS organisations: verify alignment with NHS Identity Verification and Authentication Standard DCB3051 and NHS CIS2 as part of governance mapping.

metric.name: Anchor Diversity Index
metric.description: Measures the geographic, organisational, and cultural spread of trust anchors across the trust graph. A higher score indicates greater decentralisation and resilience to collusion.

metric.name: Time to Revocation Notice (SLA)
metric.description: The elapsed time between a revocation decision and formal notification to the affected member. Lower is better for due process compliance.

metric.name: VRC Reciprocity Rate
metric.description: Proportion of VMC issuances where a valid reciprocal VRC exchange was confirmed. A low rate indicates PEP enforcement failures.

metric.name: IDVC Issuer Verification Rate
metric.description: Proportion of Phase 4 admissions where the IDVP DID was verified against the trust registry before VMC issuance. Should be 100%.

metric.name: Anomaly Detection Hit Rate (Vouching Patterns)
metric.description: Rate at which coordinated or anomalous vouching patterns are flagged by the VTA analytics engine. Higher is better for Sybil resistance.

metric.name: Registry Write Authorisation Failure Rate
metric.description: Rate at which single-party registry write attempts are rejected. Should be 100% — any successful single-party write is a governance failure.

metric.name: Appeals Process Response Time
metric.description: Median time from appeal submission to formal response from the governing body. Lower indicates a more effective due process mechanism.

metric.name: Agent Credential Scope Violation Rate
metric.description: Rate at which AI agents attempt operations outside their delegated credential scope. Any non-zero rate indicates a governance or enforcement failure.

metric.name: ZKP / Selective Disclosure Uptake Rate
metric.description: Proportion of Phase 4 applicants using privacy-preserving proofing options rather than raw IDVC disclosure. Higher indicates better privacy protection.

metric.name: Jurisdictional Concentration of Key Parties
metric.description: Proportion of trust anchors and IDVPs located within a single legal jurisdiction. Lower is better — high concentration indicates coercion risk.

metric.name: Bad-Faith Appeals Rate
metric.description: Proportion of appeal submissions subsequently determined to be coordinated or bad-faith. Rate-limiting and CIB detection should suppress this.

metric.name: Member Admission Denial Rate
metric.description: Proportion of well-formed membership applications that are denied. A high rate may indicate discriminatory gatekeeping; a very low rate may indicate weak admission enforcement.

metric.name: Credential Expiry-to-Renewal Latency
metric.description: Time between credential expiry notification and successful renewal. Relevant for both human members and AI agents. Longer latency increases operational disruption.

metric.name: Sybil Cluster Detection Rate
metric.description: Rate at which coordinated multi-M-DID registration attempts are identified and blocked. A primary uniqueness enforcement metric.

metric.name: DID Document Integrity Verification Rate
metric.description: Proportion of DID document resolutions where the VTA confirms document integrity before relying on the resolved content. Should be 100%.

metric.name: Governance Body Response Time to Security Findings
metric.description: Elapsed time from submission of a security researcher's findings to formal governance acknowledgement and response. Lower supports responsible disclosure and trust.

metric.name: Cross-VTC Revocation Contamination Rate
metric.description: Rate at which a revocation in one VTC propagates (intentionally or accidentally) to unrelated VTCs where the member holds credentials. Should be governed and scoped.

metric.name: Rate-Limiting Trigger Accuracy (AI / Non-Human)
metric.description: Proportion of rate-limiting events that correctly target non-human or adversarial activity, avoiding false positives on legitimate benign agents.

metric.name: Ceremony Completion Rate
metric.description: Proportion of initiated witnessed VRC ceremonies that reach COMPLETE or COMPLETE_WITH_EXCEPTIONS terminal state. Low rate indicates profile mismatch, abandonment, or bad-actor interference.

metric.name: Ceremony Profile Negotiation Cycles
metric.description: Mean number of proposal/counter-proposal rounds before AGREED state is reached. High values indicate persistent term incompatibility or bad-faith negotiation. Target: ≤ 2 rounds.

metric.name: Witness Role Coverage Rate
metric.description: Proportion of witnessed ceremonies where the VWC explicitly encodes a witness role (attestor / constitutor / guarantor). Should be 100% — absence indicates the spec gap identified in SC-14.

metric.name: Indirect Decline Rate
metric.description: Proportion of ceremony terminations resulting in INDIRECT_DECLINE (reason committed to community log; not disclosed to counterparty). Distinguishes dignity-preserving refusal from technical failure.

metric.name: Pre-Witness Verification Completion Rate
metric.description: Proportion of witnessed ceremonies where the witness independently verified both parties before issuing the VWC. Any rate below 100% indicates the social-engineering vulnerability identified in SC-15.

metric.name: Cross-VTC Dependency Resolution Rate
metric.description: Proportion of cross-VTC credential presentations where the receiving VTA successfully resolves the issuing VTC's governance framework and dependency map before accepting the credential. Should be 100%.

metric.name: Constitution Version Binding Rate
metric.description: Proportion of ceremonies where the ceremony profile explicitly references a specific governance framework version. A low rate indicates ceremonies may be validated against an incorrect or outdated governance version (see SC-25).

metric.name: Adjudication Initiation Latency
metric.description: Time from formal adjudication request submission to appointment of an independent adjudicator. Measures governance responsiveness to contested decisions.

metric.name: Agent Liveness Check Interval Compliance Rate
metric.description: Proportion of active agents whose last liveness check (operator VMC validity verification) falls within their declared behavioural commitment interval. Any rate below 100% indicates a potential harm window.

metric.name: Behavioural Commitment Breach Rate
metric.description: Rate at which active agents are observed operating outside their signed behavioural commitment parameters (rate limits, interaction scope, geographic constraints). Any non-zero rate triggers a Restore task.

metric.name: Non-Human Entity Participation Rate
metric.description: Proportion of trust task protocol invocations where at least one party is a non-human entity (IoT device, sensor network, legal-personhood natural entity). Tracks adoption of entangled model capabilities.

metric.name: VTC Dissolution Portability Completeness
metric.description: Proportion of VTC members who successfully receive a complete portability package (credentials, outcome records, endorsement history, dissolution record) within the SLA window during a VTC dissolution event.

metric.name: Supported Decision-Making Consent Flag Rate
metric.description: Proportion of admission ceremonies involving a co-signatory or guardian delegation where the supported-consent flag is correctly set and distinguishable from full substituted consent. A low rate indicates the architecture cannot represent co-signed consent without conflating it with substituted decision-making.

metric.name: Guardian-Mediated Credential Transition Rate
metric.description: Proportion of participants who transition from guardian-mediated to sole independent credential control (or vice versa) without membership discontinuity, VRC relationship loss, or re-admission requirement. Tracks capacity-transition lifecycle integrity.

metric.name: LPA Registration Completion Rate
metric.description: Proportion of VTC members who have a registered power of attorney that have successfully registered their attorney as a secondary notification recipient and scope-limited delegate in the VTC trust registry before capacity loss. A low rate indicates the LPA pre-registration pathway is inaccessible or undefined.

metric.name: Organisational Governance Conformance Rate
metric.description: Proportion of organisational VTC members (holding a C-DID) where the organisation's internal governance framework has been formally mapped to and accepted as satisfying the VTC governance conformance class. A low rate indicates the DTG architecture does not accommodate regulated organisational identities.

metric.name: Credential Interoperability Failure Rate
metric.description: Rate at which credentials issued by one organisational VTC member (e.g., an NHS Trust) are rejected or require manual verification by another organisational relying party due to implementation divergence. Tracks the practical utility of cross-organisational credential presentation.

metric.name: Age Assurance Failure Rate
metric.description: Rate at which age assurance checks produce false positives (adult incorrectly blocked) or false negatives (minor incorrectly admitted). False negatives are a non-negotiable child safety failure with criminal liability implications; false positives are a privacy and access harm. Both are tracked separately.

metric.name: Child Safety Non-Compliance Incident Rate
metric.description: Number of confirmed incidents in which a minor successfully obtained or presented a valid-appearing over-18 IDVC, whether through IDVP failure, synthetic credential generation, or architecture gap. A non-zero rate is a system-level failure requiring immediate escalation to the governance body, the relevant IDVP, and the appropriate regulatory authority (Ofcom/ICO).

user_story.function: Set up a new VTC by generating a Community DID, instantiating a Verifiable Trust Agent, and hard-coding Phase 1 bootstrapping policies
user_story.goal: Establish the community with auditable genesis policies, a time-bounded initiator authority, and a defensible governance record

user_story.function: Invite a defined set of Community Trust Anchors by issuing VTC invitation credentials scoped to the trust anchor role
user_story.goal: Build the initial trust graph with diversity-aware, policy-constrained anchor selection before opening to broader membership

user_story.function: Issue Verifiable Relationship Credentials (VRCs) to vouch for new members and respond to invitation requests from the initiator
user_story.goal: Grow the community responsibly, vouch only for people I genuinely know, and avoid becoming a single point of failure or collusion risk

user_story.function: Apply for VTC membership by presenting proof of a VTC invitation credential, two VRCs from existing members, and an IDVC from an approved IDVP
user_story.goal: Gain legitimate, privacy-preserving access to the VTC without facing discriminatory gatekeeping or disproportionate identity proofing burdens

user_story.function: Issue Identity Verification Credentials (IDVCs) to applicants after performing required identity proofing, and maintain IDVP standing in the VTC trust registry
user_story.goal: Provide reliable, privacy-preserving identity verification while minimising regulatory exposure and avoiding becoming a surveillance or data breach vector

user_story.function: Receive timely, clear notice of any revocation action, access a formal appeals process, and retain portability of credentials for use in other VTCs
user_story.goal: Avoid unjust or arbitrary revocation, protect my professional reputation, and have a fair process for contesting governance decisions

user_story.function: Run systematic stress-tests against VTC uniqueness enforcement, registry integrity, Sybil resistance, and DID resolution under adversarial conditions
user_story.goal: Identify exploitable weaknesses before malicious actors do, and produce actionable findings that improve VTC governance and cryptographic design

user_story.function: Present VTC membership credentials on behalf of my operator, autonomously request renewal prior to expiry, and log all actions for operator audit
user_story.goal: Execute delegated credential operations reliably within authorised scope, without exceeding granted permissions or persisting after operator revocation

user_story.function: Detect and block AI-mediated sybil generation, automated social engineering of trust anchors, and adversarial policy fuzzing at machine scale
user_story.goal: Ensure VTC governance and admission controls remain effective against non-human threat actors operating at speed and scale beyond human review capacity

user_story.function: Detect and prevent coordinated multi-M-DID registration, collusive anchor vouching rings, and gradual graph capture by a sophisticated adversarial actor
user_story.goal: Protect VTC integrity against large-scale identity fraud that exploits invitation thresholds and weak uniqueness enforcement

user_story.function: Detect and resist state-level coercion of trust anchors, IDVPs, or registry operators, and prevent forced credential revocation for political purposes
user_story.goal: Maintain VTC integrity and member safety against jurisdictional legal coercion, mandatory disclosure demands, and weaponised revocation
